_comment: PRE-EXISTING hazards in scripts that are NOT in the execution package, recorded 2026-08-02
when the guard's coverage went from 4 hand-listed files to all 50 in the directory.
WHY A BASELINE AND NOT A FIX. These are staging, provisioning and probe scripts that the
Owner runs elevated, by hand, one at a time. Editing twelve of them in a round whose stated
scope was one measurement tool would be changing code nobody asked about, in scripts whose
failure modes are the Owner's session rather than a canary. They are recorded instead, with
exact file and line, so the decision to spend a round on them is his.
WHAT THIS FILE CANNOT DO. It cannot hide a NEW hazard: the test asserts current findings are
a SUBSET of this list. Fixing one keeps the test green; adding one turns it red. It also
cannot cover a packaged script - a hazard in any of the 13 files a canary actually runs is a
hard failure and can never be baselined, which is asserted separately.
Keys are kind:line[:variable:operation] so a line number that moves shows up as new.
recordedBecause: guard coverage widened from 4 files to the whole directory after Operator-MeasureNotepadLaunch.ps1 died at line 65 on a hazard the guard never scanned for
